structuralDecisions.decision: reagent-map-visual.spec.ts lives alongside the existing reagent-map-*.spec.ts siblings in apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/tests/, not in a new directory or package.
structuralDecisions.rationale: playwright.config.ts's chromium project already testIgnores '**/reagent-map-*.spec.ts', and the 'chrome' project (via scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.sh) already picks up every file matching that glob. Matching the naming convention gets the new spec into both projects' routing for free — no config change needed for routing.

structuralDecisions.decision: Add a visible, stable error-state element to ReagentMapView.vue: a div with data-testid="reagent-map-error" and role="alert", set via a new ref immediately before the existing `throw sitesResult.reason` in onMounted, rendered in the template guarded by that ref.
structuralDecisions.rationale: No error-state element exists today (onMounted only rethrows). This is additive DOM in the existing template — it does not touch buildViewer(), the camera, newViewer.destroy(), or the Promise.allSettled control flow reagent-map-resilience.spec.ts already asserts against. Naming matches the existing data-testid="reagent-site-list" convention; role="alert" matches the accessibility pattern already used on #cesiumContainer (role="img"/aria-label).
tradeOffs: Touches a file reagent-map-resilience.spec.ts already covers in detail — any edit here re-risks that spec's zero-canvas/zero-list-item assertions if not placed carefully before the throw.
Reversibility: Cheap — it's additive markup with no behavioral coupling; removing the element later does not affect the throw/destroy control flow.

fitness.property: reagent-map-resilience.spec.ts's existing assertions (seam absent, zero canvas, zero list items) still pass unchanged after the element is added, and a new assertion confirms the element is visible with role=alert when the sites fetch rejects.
fitness.verification: Playwright run of reagent-map-resilience.spec.ts (existing) plus the new error-state @visual test in reagent-map-visual.spec.ts, both under --project=chrome.

structuralDecisions.decision: playwright.config.ts gets a new exported resolveRunnerVariant(): string | undefined that reads process.env.RUNNER_VARIANT at call time, and the config's snapshotPathTemplate is set to '.playwright-baselines/{arg}{ext}' where {arg} composes resolveRunnerVariant() with Playwright's own snapshot name token.
structuralDecisions.rationale: This mirrors the exact shape of resolveRunnerSlowMo()/resolveRunnerVideo() already in this file — exported, read-env-at-call-time, unit-tested in tests/playwright-config.spec.ts. No new config pattern is introduced; RUNNER_VARIANT just joins the two existing per-call env resolvers.

fitness.property: resolveRunnerVariant() resolves to 'debian' or 'ubi9' when RUNNER_VARIANT is set to that value, and to undefined (or a value that makes the @visual skip condition true) when unset — read fresh per call, not cached at config load.
fitness.verification: tests/playwright-config.spec.ts gains cases for resolveRunnerVariant() in the same block structure as the existing resolveRunnerSlowMo/resolveRunnerVideo test cases (lines ~68-98).

structuralDecisions.decision: apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/.playwright-baselines/{debian,ubi9}/ is a new committed directory holding only baseline PNGs, written exclusively by a --update-baselines-triggered Playwright run. No new package.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Keeps baselines colocated with the app they belong to, per-runner-image, consistent with how playwright-report and other app-local test artifacts are already scoped under apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/.

structuralDecisions.decision: scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.sh's parse_args must be restructured from a single-positional `case "${1:-}"` into a loop over "$@" so --update-baselines and --ubi9 compose in either order, each setting an independent flag (VARIANT/IMAGE_TAG/PNPM_STORE_VOLUME for --ubi9; a new UPDATE_BASELINES=1 for --update-baselines).
structuralDecisions.rationale: The current parse_args only inspects $1 and treats any second value as an error — it cannot accept two flags today. This is a required correctness change, not an optional cleanup: without it, '--ubi9 --update-baselines' hits the existing unknown-argument branch and exits 64.
tradeOffs: Widens parse_args's surface — must keep it under the complexity-6 budget (design-principles.md); split into one small helper per flag if the loop body grows past a simple case per token.
Reversibility: Cheap — purely internal to one script, covered immediately by ui-suite-in-chrome.test.sh's existing exit-code-contract pattern.

fitness.property: Both orderings (--ubi9 --update-baselines and --update-baselines --ubi9) set VARIANT=ubi9/IMAGE_TAG=saturday-runner:ubi9 AND enable baseline updates; --update-baselines alone keeps the debian default; an unrecognized third argument still exits 64 with the existing usage message.
fitness.verification: bash scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.test.sh — new test_update_baselines_composes_with_ubi9 case(s) using the existing FAKE_DOCKER_LOG assertion pattern.

structuralDecisions.decision: start_container() exports RUNNER_VARIANT into the container (alongside the existing RUNNER_SLOW_MO/RUNNER_VIDEO -e flags), and run_chrome_suite() takes the update-baselines flag as a parameter, appending --update-snapshots to the `npx playwright test --project=chrome --workers=3` invocation only when it is set.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Matches the existing -e RUNNER_SLOW_MO=... / -e RUNNER_VIDEO=... pattern in start_container() exactly. Gating --update-snapshots behind an explicit parameter (not a free env-var read inside run_chrome_suite) keeps the 'never write a baseline without the flag' invariant checkable by reading one call site.

fitness.property: RUNNER_VARIANT=debian|ubi9 appears in the docker run env flags for every invocation; --update-snapshots appears in the docker exec'd playwright command if and only if --update-baselines was passed.
fitness.verification: bash scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.test.sh — FAKE_DOCKER_LOG assertions, extending the existing test_ubi9_variant/test_default_variant_is_debian pattern with a RUNNER_VARIANT check and a new case for --update-snapshots presence/absence.

structuralDecisions.decision: Every @visual test in reagent-map-visual.spec.ts calls test.skip(!process.env.RUNNER_VARIANT, '<reason>') (or an equivalent beforeEach guard) as its first statement — never a conditional inside the assertion body — so a missing baseline fails loudly whenever RUNNER_VARIANT is set, and the whole file no-ops cleanly on a developer Mac.
structuralDecisions.rationale: AC5 requires skip-when-unset and never-skip-when-set as a hard behavioral contract, not an incidental side effect of some other check. A single, consistently-placed skip call per test is the only shape that is easy to verify by reading the file and easy for code-reviewer to catch a violation of.

fitness.property: Running the suite with RUNNER_VARIANT unset reports every @visual test as 'skipped' with a stated reason; running it with RUNNER_VARIANT set and a baseline deliberately removed reports that test as 'failed', never 'skipped'.
fitness.verification: Two manual Playwright runs recorded in the delivery record: one with RUNNER_VARIANT unset (expect all @visual tests skipped), one with RUNNER_VARIANT set and a baseline temporarily removed (expect that test failed, not skipped).

structuralDecisions.decision: The globe canvas test's tolerance is a single named constant (e.g. GLOBE_MAX_DIFF_PIXEL_RATIO = 0.01) passed into toHaveScreenshot(), never a literal repeated at the call site, and this value is never edited upward — per AC3, a flaky globe test is removed and masked instead of its tolerance being raised.
structuralDecisions.rationale: A named constant makes the 1% ceiling a single line code-reviewer can check on every future diff to this file, rather than a convention that has to be remembered. Making this a wired CI fitness function (e.g. a grep-based lint rule) is not proposed here — Approval Gate #7 would require wiring a new CI check for a one-constant invariant that code-reviewer can already catch by inspection every time this file changes, which is a worse cost/benefit than the judgment-only route.
